thread:
Maya K: started a canary run for a seq-length strata routing change (strata = [0-256,257-512,513-768,769-1024,1025+]). noticed an unexpected tail latency bump in the 769-1024 band after the runtime started preferring the Ampere-optimized kernel for decode when KV cache is hot. p95 up ~11% vs baseline. attaching quick notes below.

Luca R: can you paste the perfbot run summary?

Perf Bot: ci/perf/3087654321 - run summary
```
model: rwlm-13b-q4
hw: ampere-256 vs h100-32
workload: 70% prefill (avg len 480), 30% decode (avg decode 150)
ampere-decode-prefill-hot: p50 18ms p95 62ms p99 120ms
h100-decode-prefill-hot: p50 16ms p95 56ms p99 110ms
baseline (hysteresis=on): p95 56ms
experiment (hysteresis=off, auto-pick on seqlen): p95 62ms (+11%), p99 +9%
throughput unchanged within noise (±3%)
KV eviction spike correlated with microburst @ 12:03:22 (timestamp).
```

Samir Patel: hmm. is the routing policy the only change? were batching windows or batcher timeouts adjusted?

Maya K: no batching changes. the switch was: disable_hysteresis=true in seqlen-router and enable architecture-aware kernel preference: prefer_ampere_for_decode=true when seqlen > 768. this makes the route decision solely seqlen+arch, ignoring recent kernel success rates.

Luca R: that explains flip-flopping at the 769 boundary. if some requests prefill with cold KV then decode hits warm KV, kernel choice differs when kv_hit_rate changes. we should be careful when the decision surface depends on both seqlen and runtime state.

Ava Chen: proposal: add a short-lived smoothing window for kernel pick decisions so we don't flip inside a single request lifecycle. e.g. require kernel_preference to be stable for 3 consecutive requests or add hysteresis band 700-900.

Maya K: agreed. also saw KV KPI: during the run eviction_rate jumped 4x for the 769-1024 group. log snippet: 
```
[12:03:22] route=decode; seq=812; kv_hit=0.87; kv_evictions=42; kernel=ampere-opt; batch_ms=2.1
[12:03:22] route=prefill; seq=812; kv_hit=0.12; kernel=h100-fallback; batch_ms=1.9
```
This shows prefill used fallback path but decode used ampere path leading to cache thrash when both share pools.

Samir Patel: can we attribute p95 regression to kernel micro-ops mismatch vs just KV contention? any flamegraphs?

Maya K: captured a quick perf trace. short excerpt: 
```
ampere-decode: kernel_ms_breakdown = {matmul: 58%, load_kv: 22%, memcpy: 10%, sync: 10%}
h100-decode: kernel_ms_breakdown = {matmul: 62%, load_kv: 18%, memcpy: 8%, sync: 12%}
ampere had higher load_kv variance under eviction, causing tail.
```

Luca R: interesting — so ampere kernel has slightly worse tail for load_kv under eviction. combined with flip at 769 causes some requests to get the worse tail path. Solution directions: 1) reinstate hysteresis, 2) make kernel pick aware of recent kv_hit_rate (e.g., prefer kernel X only if kv_hit_rate>threshold), 3) isolate prefill/decode memory pools to avoid shared evictions.

Ava Chen: operationally I want two quick changes: add telemetry field kernel_pick_reason (enum: seqlen_rule, kv_metric, fallback, manual) so we can correlate picks to outcomes; and add an A/B canary that pins the decode kernel to the non-ampere variant for the 769-1024 band to confirm regression attribution.

Maya K: will run the pinned canary across both Ampere and H100 nodes. plan: run 30k requests with skewed seqlen distribution, collect p50/p95/p99+kv histograms.

Perf Bot: scheduled canary job ci/perf/3087654321-pin-canary (ETA 30m).

Samir Patel: if canary confirms, let's land the short-term fix: re-enable hysteresis + add pick_reason telemetry. medium-term: consider a tiny ML classifier for pick that ingests {seqlen, kv_hit_rate, recent_kernel_success_rate, hw_type}.

Maya K: noted. created follow-up tasks:
- add kernel_pick_reason tag to logs (owner: Maya)
- re-enable hysteresis default (owner: Luca)
- run pinned canary and share traces (owner: Maya)
- evaluate isolating prefill/decode pools (owner: Samir)

Luca R: I'll also add a quick unit test in the routing layer that simulates alternating kv_hit_rate to ensure no per-request flip.

Ava Chen: nice. please post canary link when ready and add a short blameless note to eng-runtime if we need a rollback. :thumbsup:

Maya K: will do. thanks everyone. :rocket:
